newsitem.title: CHINA: China sedan output only 45 pct of capacity - paper.
newsitem.headline: China sedan output only 45 pct of capacity - paper.

text.p: China's sedan output in 1996 was only 45 percent of capacity and production for the automobile sector as a whole was far below official estimates, the China Business Times said on Thursday.
Figures from the Ministry of Machine-Building Industry had shown automobile production last year was at 75 percent of a capacity of more than two million vehicles, the newspaper said.
"In reality, the actual rate of use of China's automobile production capacity is far, far less than those statistics," the newspaper said.
Production of sedans was just 45 percent of capacity, output of light vehicles stood at less than half of capacity and that of medium-sized vehicles was just 62 percent, it said.
Chinese auto-makers had failed to meet a state-set target of 1.55 million vehicles in 1996, producing 1.456 million cars and selling only 1.439 million of those, it said.
Much of the problem was because China had more than 300 factories making whole vehicles, it said, adding that China should ideally have seven or eight automobile groups to ensure economies of scale.
Authorities had ordered the closure of 30 factories with outputs of less than 100 vehicles a year and were trying to promote more mergers, it said without elaborating.
Domestic vehicles were also facing fiercer competition from imports and joint venture cars produced in China, it said.
